subject.title: RFC: policy on agent-directed instruction content in docs

question: Should ClawHub adopt a public acceptability rule for agent-directed instructions in SKILL.md/README content, and where should that rule live?
rationale: Current main only has adjacent execution, disclosure, and scanner-coherence guidance; the requested line would define marketplace trust policy and security-review expectations.

options.title: Accept as policy work
options.body: Add concise allowed, needs-review, and not-allowed examples to public acceptable-use or publishing docs and mirror the reviewer invariant in specs.

options.title: Fold into related RFCs
options.body: Resolve this boundary together with the declared-capability and cross-asset pipeline RFCs so declaration, detection, and policy use one model.

options.title: Keep internal for now
options.body: Leave agent-directed instruction handling as internal ClawScan/moderator judgment without promising a public rule yet.

recommendation.title: Accept as policy work
recommendation.body: Add concise allowed, needs-review, and not-allowed examples to public acceptable-use or publishing docs and mirror the reviewer invariant in specs.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is CODEOWNERS-listed for both the public policy docs and ClawScan prompt paths that would need to agree on this boundary.
